steps.title: Set up the independent kernel lab
steps.action: Create the kernel-course repository, run the supplied CPU decoder fixture, and map the tensors you will optimize.
steps.evidence: A local CPU smoke, fixed configuration and random state dict, and one dimensioned decoder diagram.

steps.title: Freeze environments, measurement rules, and spending limits
steps.action: Write the local/NVIDIA/H100 environment plan and a bounded measurement contract before renting a GPU.
steps.evidence: `reports/kernels/environment-plan.md` and a spending ledger with a shutdown checklist.

steps.title: Model GPU Indexing and Memory Traffic Locally
steps.action: Execute a Python shape-and-traffic calculator, then map it to GPU execution and memory.
steps.evidence: A working local calculator, dimensioned table and three bottleneck hypotheses.

steps.title: Prepare a Bounded Profiling Session
steps.action: Smoke-test a pinned 4090 environment and the tiny decoder; record versions. Timebox setup, preserving a precise blocker if the image fails.
steps.evidence: Working smoke command and hardware manifest, or documented setup blocker.

steps.title: Build Reliable GPU Timing Utilities
steps.action: Implement warm-up, synchronization, and repeated timing; separate compilation, transfers, and steady-state execution. Check one deliberately incorrect asynchronous measurement.
steps.evidence: Timing utility and explained discrepancy between valid and invalid measurements.

steps.title: Profile and Explain Dominant Operations
steps.action: Capture a short decoder profile; estimate FLOPs and bytes for the three dominant operations, then compare measurements with your predictions.
steps.evidence: Three-operation bottleneck table with measurements, estimates, and separate MPS results if used.

steps.title: Write CUDA Vector Addition Indexing
steps.action: Read only the needed CUDA/vector-add material; write thread indexing and a minimal wrapper using the working remote environment.
steps.evidence: CUDA launch and indexing explained for a small contiguous vector.

steps.title: Validate CUDA Boundaries and Timing
steps.action: Handle non-multiple lengths and launch bounds; compare outputs with PyTorch and record synchronized timing with compilation excluded.
steps.evidence: CUDA agreement on ordinary and boundary lengths; separate compilation timing.

steps.title: Implement Triton Vector Addition Masks
steps.action: Implement Triton program IDs, offsets, and masked loads/stores; reuse the same inputs and reference from the CUDA exercise.
steps.evidence: Triton vector addition passes ordinary and non-multiple lengths.

steps.title: Compare Both Vector Addition Implementations
steps.action: Run the common correctness matrix and steady-state timing for CUDA, Triton, and PyTorch; explain launch overhead and memory traffic.
steps.evidence: Both kernels pass; timing table separates compilation and steady-state execution.

steps.title: Derive Stable Row Softmax
steps.action: Read K3's softmax section; derive max subtraction and reduction shapes, then define supported row widths and extreme-logit cases.
steps.evidence: Stable formula, bytes estimate, and a fixed correctness matrix.

steps.title: Implement Triton Softmax Reductions
steps.action: Write masked row loads, FP32 reduction, exponentiation, normalization, and stores; first validate small power-of-two rows.
steps.evidence: Small-row outputs match the controlled-precision reference.

steps.title: Handle Softmax Tails and Extremes
steps.action: Repair masking and numerical behavior for non-power-of-two widths, repeated values, and extreme finite logits; record supported inputs.
steps.evidence: Tail and extreme-logit cases pass without unexplained nonfinite values.

steps.title: Benchmark Softmax Against Both Baselines
steps.action: Measure eager, compiled, and Triton softmax across fixed shapes using warm-up and repeated synchronized batches; interpret bytes moved.
steps.evidence: Correctness matrix and fair timing table with bandwidth interpretation.

steps.title: Specify RMSNorm Precision and Shapes
steps.action: Derive RMSNorm's reduction and scaling; define epsilon, supported layouts, row counts, widths, and accumulation dtype before coding.
steps.evidence: Explicit supported-shape contract and reference calculations.

steps.title: Implement Triton RMSNorm Forward
steps.action: Implement masked row loads, FP32 square-mean accumulation, reciprocal square root, scaling, and stores; compare small inputs with PyTorch.
steps.evidence: Forward outputs agree on small supported shapes.

steps.title: Validate RMSNorm Across Row Shapes
steps.action: Check boundary widths, varied row counts, zeros, repeated values, and supported dtypes; report errors against the reference.
steps.evidence: Error table covers the declared support and precision contract.

steps.title: Measure RMSNorm Wins and Losses
steps.action: Benchmark eager, compiled, and custom RMSNorm under consistent precision; retain regressions and explain likely memory or launch bottlenecks.
steps.evidence: Validated support matrix and timing table containing wins and losses.

steps.title: Review execution, reductions, and benchmark validity
steps.action: Audit vector add, softmax, and RMSNorm using a closed-book explanation and one targeted numerical check.
steps.evidence: `review-2.md` with a memory diagram, masked-row example, and an honest benchmark audit.

steps.title: Repair a blocker or consolidate
steps.action: Use the scheduled hour for an unfinished check or targeted retrieval. Finish early when current.
steps.evidence: A resolved blocker or minimal reproducer, and a precise next action.

steps.title: Derive Tiled Matrix Multiplication
steps.action: Read K3's matmul section; map program IDs, block indices, strides, and the reduction dimension to a tiny numerical example.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned tile diagram and controlled-precision reference.

steps.title: Implement Triton Matmul Tile Loop
steps.action: Write masked A/B tile loads, dot products, and FP32 accumulators; initially restrict dimensions to exact tile multiples.
steps.evidence: Exact-tile matrix products match the reference.

steps.title: Support Matmul Boundaries and Strides
steps.action: Add tail masks and supported stride handling; check dimensions on both sides of tile boundaries and document unsupported layouts.
steps.evidence: Boundary-shape comparisons pass under the stated layout contract.

steps.title: Validate Tensor Core Matmul Precision
steps.action: Check the selected tensor-core path and precision settings; run the frozen random/boundary matrix and document numerical tolerances.
steps.evidence: Random and boundary comparisons pass against a matched-precision reference.

steps.title: Freeze Matmul Tuning and Baselines
steps.action: Choose a small tile search before measuring; prepare `torch.matmul` and compiled-composition baselines with matching precision and resident inputs.
steps.evidence: Predeclared tiles, shapes, and baseline settings.

steps.title: Measure Tile Reuse and Occupancy
steps.action: Run the bounded tile search using repeated synchronized batches; inspect the strongest and weakest configurations without expanding the search.
steps.evidence: Tile timing table with median, variability, and reuse observations.

steps.title: Fuse One Matmul Output Epilogue
steps.action: Add a column-bias epilogue to the FP32 accumulator before the final output cast; verify against an explicit reference with matching accumulation and cast order before benchmarking.
steps.evidence: Supported zero, nonconstant and tail-bias cases match the explicit reference with the same accumulation and output-cast order.

steps.title: Explain Matmul Performance Tradeoffs Clearly
steps.action: Compare the fused kernel with library matmul and compiled composition; explain reuse, occupancy, and measured regressions without requiring a library win.
steps.evidence: Final timing table and supported conclusions about reuse and occupancy.

steps.title: Derive Online Softmax State Updates
steps.action: Read the required K4 sections; derive running maximum, normalizer, and weighted-output updates when a new score tile arrives.
steps.evidence: Written recurrence with dimensions and rescaling factors.

steps.title: Verify Online Softmax Tile Merges
steps.action: Implement the recurrence on tiny PyTorch vectors; compare different tile partitions with dense softmax and inspect extreme finite values.
steps.evidence: Tile-merge results match dense normalization.

steps.title: Implement Blockwise Causal Attention Reference
steps.action: Apply the verified recurrence to Q/K/V blocks with causal masking, avoiding storage of the full score matrix.
steps.evidence: Small causal attention outputs agree with the dense reference.

steps.title: Validate Attention Recurrence and Memory
steps.action: Run varied small lengths and tile boundaries; explain causal masks, online state, and memory accounting in a concise derivation.
steps.evidence: Dense-reference parity plus explained recurrence and memory savings.

steps.title: Specify Restricted Triton Attention Forward
steps.action: Fix one head dimension, bounded lengths, dtype, and causal convention; map the blockwise reference to Triton tiles using K3/K4.
steps.evidence: Restricted support contract and tile/state mapping.

steps.title: Implement Attention Tiles and Online State
steps.action: Translate Q/K/V loading and the online normalization update to Triton; debug a tiny exact-tile case against the existing reference.
steps.evidence: A tiny supported attention case matches dense output.

steps.title: Validate Attention Causality and Tails
steps.action: Add supported tail and causal masks; check numerical errors and nonfinite values. Narrow the shape family if needed, preserving an honest completion gate.
steps.evidence: Causal and tail tests pass without NaNs on declared inputs.

steps.title: Benchmark Restricted Attention Forward Correctness
steps.action: Compare validated outputs, peak memory, and latency with dense attention and SDPA. If correctness remains unresolved, record the blocker and extend the lab.
steps.evidence: Working restricted forward with correctness, latency, and memory results; backward remains optional.

steps.title: Review tiled matmul and online attention
steps.action: Reconstruct a tile and online-softmax merge, then audit one causal boundary case.
steps.evidence: `review-4.md` with dimensioned tile addresses, a worked merge, and a supported-shape audit.

steps.title: Repair a blocker or consolidate
steps.action: Use the scheduled hour for an unfinished check or targeted retrieval. Finish early when current.
steps.evidence: A resolved blocker or minimal reproducer, and a precise next action.

steps.title: Derive RMSNorm Input and Weight Gradients
steps.action: Derive input and weight gradients, including reduction axes and epsilon; check the algebra using a small high-precision PyTorch reference.
steps.evidence: Dimensioned backward equations and a validated reference.

steps.title: Implement RMSNorm Input Gradient Kernel
steps.action: Translate the input-gradient reduction to Triton; test small supported shapes and inspect accumulation precision against the reference.
steps.evidence: Input gradients agree on small supported GPU cases.

steps.title: Implement RMSNorm Weight Gradient Reduction
steps.action: Implement weight-gradient accumulation and reduction for the documented shape family; compare input and weight gradients across boundary shapes.
steps.evidence: GPU input and weight gradients pass boundary-shape comparisons.

steps.title: Validate Actual GPU Gradient Dtypes
steps.action: Run the supported-dtype gradient matrix, recording errors and tolerances separately from high-precision derivative checks; repair demonstrated discrepancies.
steps.evidence: Actual GPU input/weight gradient agreement across the declared dtype and shape contract.

steps.title: Register the Custom Triton Operator
steps.action: Read K5 for the pinned PyTorch version; register RMSNorm forward and its metadata using the supported custom-operator interface.
steps.evidence: Registered forward operator executes with documented metadata.

steps.title: Connect Autograd and Unsupported Cases
steps.action: Register the backward path; add explicit fallback or rejection for unsupported layouts, shapes, or dtypes, then exercise each branch.
steps.evidence: Autograd works and unsupported cases fail clearly or use the documented fallback.

steps.title: Integrate RMSNorm Into the Decoder
steps.action: Replace the decoder's reference RMSNorm through one configuration switch; compare training loss and representative parameter gradients under shared weights.
steps.evidence: Decoder training-loss and gradient parity with the reference path.

steps.title: Profile Integration and Amdahl Limits
steps.action: Profile the decoder before and after integration under identical conditions; calculate the maximum expected gain from the original operator share.
steps.evidence: Parity gate, before/after profile, and an explained Amdahl calculation.

steps.title: Prepare the Pallas Hopper Environment
steps.action: Timebox H100 setup and the official K6 smoke test; record package/backend versions. Preserve installation blockers rather than substituting CPU interpretation.
steps.evidence: Actual H100 smoke output and environment manifest, or explicit unresolved blocker.

steps.title: Map Pallas Refs Grids and Memory
steps.action: Read the needed K6 sections; trace Refs, launch grids, memory spaces, and synchronization through the working GPU quickstart.
steps.evidence: Annotated quickstart explaining memory movement and synchronization.

steps.title: Port One Row Kernel to Pallas
steps.action: Port the existing softmax or RMSNorm forward reference to Pallas for a restricted shape family; run the smallest actual GPU case.
steps.evidence: A real H100 Pallas kernel produces the expected small-case output.

steps.title: Validate the Pallas GPU Kernel
steps.action: Compare with JAX across the declared shapes and dtypes; inspect tails and numerical errors. Extend the lab if actual GPU correctness remains blocked.
steps.evidence: One actual Pallas GPU kernel agrees with JAX across its supported contract.

steps.title: Benchmark Pallas Against Jitted JAX
steps.action: Measure the existing kernel and `jax.jit` baseline on the same H100; use `block_until_ready` and separate compilation from warmed execution.
steps.evidence: Matched error/timing table with compile and execute costs separated.

steps.title: Trace Hopper Pipelined Matmul Stages
steps.action: Walk through K6's official matmul example; map global-memory transfers, shared-memory buffers, computation, and synchronization without adding a required kernel.
steps.evidence: Annotated pipeline identifying stages and buffer lifetimes.

steps.title: Study Modern Attention Hardware Tradeoffs
steps.action: Read selected FA4/CuTe material in K7; explain how hardware and scheduling choices differ from your restricted attention implementation.
steps.evidence: Short comparison tied to code paths and hardware bottlenecks.

steps.title: Explain Pallas Timing and Staging
steps.action: Review the benchmark for asynchronous timing errors; finalize the error table and explain staged memory movement from the official walkthrough.
steps.evidence: Validated timing/error table and clear staged-memory explanation.

steps.title: Review differentiation, integration, and Pallas evidence
steps.action: Defend the RMSNorm derivative and audit framework integration alongside the actual H100 result.
steps.evidence: `review-6.md` with a gradient derivation, branch table, and separated Pallas compile/execute evidence.

steps.title: Repair a blocker or consolidate
steps.action: Use the scheduled hour for an unfinished check or targeted retrieval. Finish early when current.
steps.evidence: A resolved blocker or minimal reproducer, and a precise next action.

steps.title: Freeze End To End Decoder Measurements
steps.action: Specify eager/compiled modes, kernel switch, sequence lengths, prefill/decode cases, precision, and transfer boundaries before collecting results.
steps.evidence: Frozen experiment matrix and equivalent model configurations.

steps.title: Measure Decoder Prefill and Transfers
steps.action: Measure prefill with and without the custom kernel; separate host/device transfer, compilation, cold execution, and warmed execution.
steps.evidence: Prefill timings with distinct setup, transfer, and steady-state costs.

steps.title: Measure Cached Decode Across Lengths
steps.action: Run the same kernel comparison for cached decode across several prompt lengths, using equivalent inputs and repeated synchronized batches.
steps.evidence: Decode timing table with variability and unchanged correctness.

steps.title: Report Whole Model Gains and Regressions
steps.action: Check measurement consistency and summarize the complete decoder results; retain slowdowns and explain why isolated-kernel changes may have small effects.
steps.evidence: Whole-model results across lengths, including prefill/decode and retained regressions.

steps.title: Inspect One Optional Kernel DSL
steps.action: Inspect one CuTe/FA4 or Helion example. An optional install/benchmark shares this hour; stop at the limit and document blockers if it fails.
steps.evidence: Current-tooling note; optional installation success is not required.

steps.title: Recreate the Main Kernel Environment
steps.action: Use the existing environment manifest to prepare a clean reproduction of the main kernel result; identify dependency or command fragility.
steps.evidence: Clean environment attempt with exact versions and setup issues.

steps.title: Repair Reproduction Commands and Dependencies
steps.action: Fix only identified setup fragility and rerun the correctness smoke test; keep the main benchmark configuration unchanged.
steps.evidence: Documented commands recreate the validated benchmark configuration.

steps.title: Reproduce the Main Kernel Result
steps.action: Run the main benchmark from the clean setup; compare errors and timings with recorded results, explaining material differences.
steps.evidence: Repeatable benchmark plus current-tooling note and disclosed environment differences.

steps.title: Audit Remaining Kernel Measurement Risks
steps.action: Inspect existing results for specific noise or correctness gaps; list only the reruns needed and verify common baseline precision settings.
steps.evidence: Bounded rerun list tied to concrete unresolved risks.

steps.title: Resolve Identified Benchmark Noise Gaps
steps.action: Execute the justified repeated measurements under consistent conditions; retain raw batches and record machine or thermal variability.
steps.evidence: Raw measurements resolve or clearly delimit the listed noise risks.

steps.title: Complete Shape Support and Precision Matrix
steps.action: Fill missing entries in the declared shape/dtype contract using focused checks; mark unsupported cases and preserve operation-specific tolerances.
steps.evidence: Complete support/error matrix with explicit unsupported cases.

steps.title: Verify Plotting and Hardware Provenance
steps.action: Regenerate plots from saved raw data; confirm hardware manifests, baseline settings, and correctness evidence agree across the report.
steps.evidence: Raw data, reproducible plotting command, hardware manifest, and consistent baseline settings.

steps.title: Draft the Kernel Systems Report
steps.action: Write the main result and methodology from existing evidence, including correctness, strong baselines, whole-model impact, and limitations.
steps.evidence: Report draft with claims traceable to raw measurements.

steps.title: Build a Minimal Reproducer and Focused Fix
steps.action: Reduce one observed behavior to an executable case, then prepare a minimal fix or support-boundary test.
steps.evidence: Smallest reproducer plus a focused diff or documented limitation check.

steps.title: Verify the Regression or Support Boundary
steps.action: Test the focused change before and after, or validate the explicitly documented rejection/fallback.
steps.evidence: Reproducible behavior and precise before/after or limitation evidence.

steps.title: Finalize Systems Evidence and Contribution
steps.action: Review the report and prepared contribution or internal finding; state supported hardware, measured limitations and the actual observed result.
steps.evidence: Systems report and review-ready evidence package with accurate scope.

steps.title: Repair a blocker or consolidate
steps.action: Use the scheduled hour for an unfinished check or targeted retrieval. Finish early when current.
steps.evidence: A resolved blocker or minimal reproducer, and a precise next action.

steps.title: Take the independent kernel assessment
steps.action: Explain and diagnose a kernel result from first principles without introducing a new implementation.
steps.evidence: `assessment.md` containing a timed explanation, one diagnosis, and an honest competency rubric.

steps.title: Verify the release candidate from a clean checkout
steps.action: Reproduce local correctness and figure generation using only the documented repository.
steps.evidence: A clean-checkout verification log and a precise list of hardware checks already completed or still pending.

steps.title: Package the kernel portfolio and contribution draft
steps.action: Package the engineering portfolio and any legitimate contribution; otherwise document the verified internal finding.
steps.evidence: A polished README, systems report, support table, and contribution or internal-reproducer index.

steps.title: Release the portfolio and choose the next systems question
steps.action: Prepare a shareable release, perform a short demonstration, and select one evidence-driven next experiment.
steps.evidence: A release checklist, five-minute demo outline, and a one-page follow-up proposal.
